title: The Sorry letter of the boy
subtitle: 互助关爱 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）
meta: 主题语境：互助关爱（社会服务与人际沟通·互助与关爱）　|　核心词汇：sorry　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 sorry 的用法与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1973 the keeper wrote of ① a sorry letter of the boy in the calendar, and everybody in the tower said at once that it was ② so sorry that nobody in the tower would go near it. Three years on, people still spoke of that morning, and of how the keeper, who never explained anything, had done it without complaint and gone home; it was the sorry ones, my mother said, that people remembered longest.

It was ③ the sorry letter of the boy that anybody there had ever seen, or so the calendar for January 1967 claims. My mother, who had seen them all, thought it ④ too sorry to be of any use to anybody, and said as much to the traveller who had come to help; the sorry ones, she used to say, were never the useful ones.

My uncle, who kept the clock at the far stair, meant something else entirely. He called the whole business ⑤ a sorry sight of the house, and said that no traveller in his right mind would call it ⑥ as sorry as the sight of the house they had once had in the old tower. He was never a man who cared whether a thing was sorry or not, and he said so.

By 1980 the matter had shrunk to half a line in the calendar. What the line asked for was ⑦ something sorry, and nothing besides. The traveller from the next tower called the whole plan ⑧ quite sorry; everybody laughed, and then did exactly what he had said. After that the calendar kept the names of the sorry ones only.

My mother said nothing at all. In 1983, with great care, she wrote of another sorry letter of the boy in the same calendar, and the work, which took two years, seemed ⑨ no less sorry than anybody had expected. ⑩ The sorry sight of the house that nobody had wanted to name, she said in 1985, was the one she could never quite name; the sorry ones, she added, are always the ones that stay.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. adj. 歉疚（前置定语 a sorry letter of the boy：1973 年守夜人在年历里记下的那件歉疚的道歉信）
B. adj. 歉疚／凄惨（两处加强说法：so sorry that … 与 no less sorry than …）
C. adj. 歉疚／凄惨（两处定语从句式的最高级说法，见第 3、10 题）
D. adj. 歉疚（表语 too sorry to do：母亲觉得它太歉疚，反倒派不上用场）
E. adj. 凄惨（前置定语 a sorry sight of the house：叔叔把整件事称作一桩凄惨的景象）
F. adj. 凄惨（同级比较 as sorry as：拿眼前这桩跟旧日那桩那座房子的凄惨景象相比）
G. adj. 凄惨（后置定语 something sorry：修饰不定代词时须放在其后）
H. adj. 凄惨（受程度副词修饰 quite sorry：那位过路人的评价）

items.q: a sorry letter of the boy
the sorry letter of the boy that
a sorry sight of the house
The sorry sight of the house that

answers.why: sorry 意为“歉疚”，1973 年守夜人在年历里记下的是“一件歉疚的道歉信”，此处作前置定语 a sorry letter of the boy。
sorry 意为“歉疚”，此处用 so sorry that 结构，说它歉疚到钟楼里没人敢靠近。
sorry 意为“歉疚”，年历上 一月 那行字说那是当地人从未见过的歉疚男孩的道歉信，等于最高级的说法。
sorry 意为“歉疚”，母亲认为这件东西“太歉疚了，谁也用不上”，too sorry to do 表示“太……以致不能”。
sorry 意为“凄惨”，叔叔把整件事称作“一桩凄惨的景象”，此处作前置定语 a sorry sight of the house。
sorry 意为“凄惨”，叔叔不肯说它“跟旧日那桩那座房子的凄惨景象一样凄惨”，同级比较用 as sorry as。
sorry 意为“凄惨”，年历上那半行字要的是“凄惨的东西”，something 被形容词修饰时形容词须后置：something sorry。
sorry 意为“凄惨”，邻钟楼来的那位过路人认为这套计划“相当凄惨”，quite 修饰原级 sorry。
sorry 意为“凄惨”，no less sorry than 表示“其凄惨不亚于……”，此处说这趟活儿之凄惨不亚于任何人的预料。
sorry 意为“凄惨”，母亲 1985 年说的是“那桩她始终叫不出名字的凄惨景象”，that 从句限定到极致。

task2.title: Task 2　语境运用
task2.intro: 请把下列句子译成英文，括号里是必须用到的形式。
items: 1973 年，守夜人在年历里记下了一件歉疚的道歉信。（a sorry letter of the boy）
它歉疚到钟楼里没有一个人敢靠近。（so sorry that …）
母亲觉得它太歉疚，谁也用不上。（too sorry to …）
叔叔把整件事称作一桩凄惨的景象。（a sorry sight of the house）
他说，谁也不会认为它跟旧日那桩那座房子的凄惨景象一样凄惨。（as sorry as …）
到了 1980 年，年历上只剩半行字：要的是一件凄惨的东西。（something sorry）
answers: In 1973 the keeper wrote of a sorry letter of the boy in the calendar.
It was so sorry that nobody in the tower would go near it.
My mother thought it too sorry to be of any use to anybody.
My uncle called the whole business a sorry sight of the house.
He said nobody would call it as sorry as the sight of the house they had once had.
By 1980 the calendar asked for nothing but something sorry.

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 sorry 的 3 种不同用法（前置定语、表语、比较级／最高级、后置定语等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1973 the keeper wrote of a sorry letter of the boy in the calendar, and nobody forgot it.
It was the sorry letter of the boy that anybody there had ever seen, or so the calendar says.
My mother thought it too sorry to be of any use, and said so plainly.
My uncle called the whole business a sorry sight of the house, and nobody argued with him.
The traveller from the next tower called the plan quite sorry, and everybody laughed.
The sorry ones, my mother said, are always the ones that stay.
